name: Client-facing counterparts and non-DPRK subcontractor roles
caveats: A foreign contractor, customer-facing counterpart, or local company needs direct evidence before the record can describe knowing or complicity.
Foreign contractors, customers, local companies, schools, universities, jurisdictions, networks, and service providers require direct evidence before treatment as knowing participants.
Preserve the difference between unwitting outsourced labor and deliberate facilitation.
Program-level 2022 guidance; it describes program controls, while team, contractor, local-company, and customer findings require case-specific sources.
This is a historical, source-qualified program-level finding; current census and person, organization, jurisdiction, platform-user or technology-user status require current sources.
This materially sharpens existing generic intermediary and subcontracting coverage by separating job acquisition, customer-facing communication, procurement, and actual task completion roles.
Treat subcontracting as one corroborating signal in a documented review process; nationality or sanctions status requires other evidence.

infrastructure.statement: The advisory states that DPRK IT workers often rely on overseas contacts to obtain freelance work and interface with customers. It further describes managers hiring non-DPRK subcontractors or teams—sometimes unaware of the employer's real identity—to complete work, make software purchases, or handle customer interactions that could expose a DPRK worker. Separately, some teams reportedly operated on paper through a legitimate local company or paid a foreign company to conceal their origin.
infrastructure.evidence_class: official intelligence, sanctions, law-enforcement, and compliance synthesis
infrastructure.historical_boundary: Program-level 2022 guidance; not a claim about every team, contractor, local company, or customer.
